question: Can a regularised linear model on HOG-style gradient features beat a pixel-based neural-network stand-in for the paper's ResNet50 on a public image set with repeated subjects, when the test split is kept within the same subjects?
method: Stratified within-subject split; standardised pixel MLP baseline vs standardised multinomial logistic regression with balanced class weights on HOG-style gradient-orientation features; 3-fold stratified CV on the training split for tuning; test set used once per seed.
baseline: Standardised pixel MLPClassifier (stand-in for the paper's ResNet50); tuned over alpha and hidden layer size.
improved: Standardised LogisticRegression with class_weight='balanced' on HOG-style cell orientation histograms; tuned over inverse regularisation strength C.
notes: Olivetti faces is a stand-in for the paper's orange images (no public orange-Brix dataset with a download link); faces are not oranges and the task is 40-way identity recognition, not sweetness regression. The MLP is not ResNet50. The test split has only about 120 images, so accuracy differences of a few points are within noise; std is over three model seeds only, with one data split. HOG-style features are a simplified numpy implementation, not skimage HOG. The previous LightGBM improved model was replaced because its CV accuracy was far below the baseline's (boosted trees overfit with ~7 images per subject).
